clue.text: Ready to bat where opener dismissed: that's made sense

indicators.note: the opener is the first in, so dismissing it sends off the first letter of the phrase

parts.note: a batsman puts on leg pads before going in

explanation.surface: A cricketer waits, pads on, after the opening batsman is out, and it all made sense.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is padded up is ready to go in; the cricketing words 'opener dismissed' double as the instruction to drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: If an account added up, its parts fitted together, so it was coherent and believable.

indicators.note: something done appallingly is botched, so these letters come out in a mess

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that the National Health Service is shockingly patchy, and the reader is told to admit it.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's state-funded National Health Service. 'is' serves twice: its letters join the fodder after NHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hit-and-miss sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails, which is to say it is unreliable.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
a girl's name
R stands for runs on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A society girl dashes off: is she a smooth operator?
explanation.definitionFit: A skater glides over ice with flowing motion, so the playful description of an easy glider fits.

clue.text: Emerge bearing child close to natural philosopher

indicators.note: to bear something is to carry it within, so the first word holds what follows

parts.note: to arise is to come up or appear
a tot is a small child

indicators.note: 'close to' keeps only the last letter of 'natural'

parts.note: the closing letter of natural

explanation.surface: A natural philosopher comes forth, carrying a baby close by.
explanation.walkthrough: The child and the last letter of 'natural' join first, then sit inside the word for emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker who wrote on physics and biology as well as ethics, a philosopher above all.

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the pieces run back the other way

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
a pen's nib does the writing

explanation.surface: An author remembers a wild spree, offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a short bout of excess, the same idea as a spree of eating, drinking or spending.

clue.text: Criminal drooled about a fabulously rich city

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order
about means around, so the reworked letters surround the next piece

parts.note: letters rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook drools over a city of fabulous wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold that Spanish explorers sought in South America, a byword for fabulous riches.

clue.text: Down this? Any number entering hole

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone peers down a hole and asks whether to go down it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' is the verb to swallow in one go, not a direction, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint of beer is the classic drink one downs in a pub, so it is the thing being gulped.

clue.text: Undercover agent in car of your dreams?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a spy planted to lie dormant until activated
second meaning: a railway carriage with beds, where one sleeps and dreams

explanation.walkthrough: 'Car of your dreams' looks like an ideal motor, but it is a railway car where you dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a dormant spy awaiting orders and the berthed carriage on an overnight train.

parts.note: afflicted means sick
Shakespeare's first name was William, Will for short

explanation.surface: Was the hostility caused by Shakespeare falling sick?
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read in reverse of the clue order: an afflicted Will is an ill Will.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is a settled feeling of animosity or enmity toward someone, the same as hostility.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A popular northern pub where the drinker hangs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is DRINKER, part of the long themed answer at 14.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub, the place a regular boozer frequents, so it is that tippler's hangout.

clue.text: Times journalist finally seen by American theologian

parts.note: eras are periods of time

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of journalist
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A writer for The Times newspaper is finally spotted by an American theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is just periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Erastus was a sixteenth-century Swiss physician and theologian who argued the state should rule the church.

clue.text: King Herod on telly frightened Dicky? He's in that Olmi film!

indicators.note: dicky is slang for unsound or shaky, so these letters are in poor order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A television King Herod scared a nervous viewer, who is cast in an Olmi film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's in' tells you to add HE to the fodder; 'Dicky' is placed as if it were the frightened person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermanno Olmi directed the 1988 Italian film The Legend of the Holy Drinker, from Joseph Roth's novella.

parts.note: under means less than enough, as in underfunded
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: Someone suffering from a lack of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffer from' reads as one phrase, but 'from' only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo an operation or hardship is to experience or endure it, much as one suffers it.

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: A scoundrel tries to get past the porter at a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: A club porter suggests a doorman, but the club is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's bag of clubs round the course, so a porter for golf clubs.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: yes-men are always willing to agree

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits into agree plus able: a yes-man can always be relied on to say yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both willing to consent and pleasing or enjoyable company.

clue.text: One girl going astray with roué is anything but 28

definitions.note: 28 is HOLY, part of the themed answer at 14

indicators.note: things going astray wander off course, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl who goes off the rails with a rake is far from saintly.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreligious means lacking religious faith or reverence, the opposite of godly and sacred.

clue.text: Topless Canterbury pilgrim in some light banter

indicators.note: without a top, so the first letter of the word is removed
in means placed inside, so the shortened word sits within another

parts.note: a ray is a beam, a little light
the Miller is a pilgrim in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, here without his first letter

explanation.surface: A topless pilgrim on the road to Canterbury exchanges light-hearted banter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Canterbury pilgrims are the tellers of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, among them the bawdy Miller.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or ridicule, which is what banter is.

clue.text: Inspirational woman in gym with unnamed doctor

indicators.note: un-named means stripped of the abbreviation for name, so that letter goes

parts.note: to doctor an animal is to neuter it; dropping the N for name leaves this
PE is physical education, gym class at school

explanation.surface: An inspiring woman at the gym with an anonymous physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician, but it is the verb meaning to neuter an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, goddess of music and lyric poetry, who inspired artists.

clue.text: What cat uses when hunting bird in south?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the bird sits within the abbreviation

parts.note: STH is a standard abbreviation for south
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A cat stalking a bird down south relies on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat creeps up on prey silently and unseen, and that furtive quiet is stealth.

clue.text: Happy maybe to receive information initially not delivered?

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: happy might be described as not sad; maybe flags the made-up word

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of information

explanation.surface: Someone is perhaps happy to get news that was never actually delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' looks like a mood, but 'maybe' warns that it stands for a coined opposite of sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech left unsaid was never spoken aloud, so it was not delivered.

clue.text: Is it the viviparous blenny Pelé suggests?

parts.note: the surface asks after a fish that bears live young
the footballer's name, put with the word out, has exactly the letters of the fish

explanation.surface: A quiz question: is this the live-bearing fish that the great Brazilian footballer has in mind?
explanation.walkthrough: Pelé is the Brazilian footballing legend; his name rearranged with the word out spells the fish, a loose hint rather than a strict mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: The eelpout Zoarces viviparus is a blenny-like fish of northern seas that gives birth to live young.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Scots word for more; Jock is slang for a Scotsman
second meaning: the first name of the film star ... West

explanation.surface: A Scotsman asks for more while out west.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a common nickname for a Scot. 'In West' means the word that sits in front of West in the actress's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Scots dialect for more and also the first name of the Hollywood actress West.

clue.text: Male 5-9 did you say? In Pagnol's work?

indicators.note: asking what you heard someone say signals that sound, not spelling, matters

parts.note: 5-9 is BINGE DRINKER; a male one is a fellow who is hooked on the sauce, slang for drink

explanation.surface: Is the male binge drinker, you ask, in Pagnol's story?
explanation.walkthrough: To be on the sauce is slang for drinking heavily; said with a French accent, man on the sauces gives the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Pagnol wrote and filmed Manon des Sources, the sequel to Jean de Florette.

indicators.note: the phrase keeps the name inside it, holding it within its run of letters

parts.note: found across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: A woman named Chloe the Lioness is being looked after by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's first name, and any female name can define a woman in crosswords.

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African nation, the largest on the continent, so a country.

explanation.definitionFit: To nab is informal for to seize or arrest, the police sense of pick up.

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A couple downing beer and a couple of cocktails, plus a glass of Italian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine after the beer, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Palermo is the capital of Sicily and a major Italian seaport.

clue.text: Russian leader embracing Eastern Time sees light

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the leader's name wraps around a letter

parts.note: Lenin led the Bolshevik revolution

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader in a time zone in the east finally sees the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sees light' reads as a phrase meaning enlightenment, but 'sees' only links and 'light' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient sentence is a light one: mild, not severe in punishment.
